title: SQL Joins: The Key to Data Relationships

scenes.line1: Why do SQL joins trip people up?
scenes.line2: What’s the one rule you must know?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why SQL joins are a common interview pitfall? What’s the one rule that makes joins click?

scenes.label: INNER
scenes.sub: Matches rows in both tables using keys.
scenes.say: First, INNER JOIN only returns rows where keys match in both tables. No match, no row.

scenes.label: LEFT
scenes.sub: Keeps all rows from the left table, fills gaps with NULLs.
scenes.say: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table, even if there’s no match. Missing data is filled in as NULL.
If you forget the join condition, you get a huge, confusing result. With outer joins, watch out for NULLs—they can trip up your logic.

scenes.question: How do you check for NULL in joins?
scenes.right: Use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL to check for missing values.
scenes.say: Here’s a classic trap: don’t use equals or not equals for NULLs. Always use IS NULL or IS NOT NULL when checking for missing values.
